title: Why MCP Exists #Shorts
description:
So software tools have been talking to each other for decades through something called APIs. API stands for Application Programming Interface. And simply put, it's just a standardized way for one piece of software to request information from another.

That's how your CRM syncs with your email. That's how Bloomberg pulls market data. That's how payment systems talk to banks. APIs are essentially the plumbing that makes modern business software work.

With respect to AI, AI had a problem. It was incredibly smart but completely disconnected from all of that plumbing. It couldn't plug into your systems where your actual work lives.

And every AI company was trying to solve this, but they were all kind of doing it differently. OpenAI had their own approach. Google had theirs. Anthropic had theirs.

If you were a tool builder—say you were trying to make a CRM or a project management app—and you wanted to connect AI, you had to build separate integrations for pretty much every single AI platform. And that doesn't really scale.

So in late 2024, Anthropic released something called MCP, Model Context Protocol, as an open standard.
